dedupe_keys.name: multi agent reinforcement learning model of market competition among wireless providers in shared spectrum

description: This paper studies competition among wireless service providers that serve customers on shared spectrum when the market demand function is initially unknown and has to be learned. Earlier models of competition with congestible resources assume known demand so providers can optimise price (Bertrand) or quantity (Cournot); here the learning is modelled by multi-agent reinforcement learning, and the authors examine whether tacit collusion appears and how its prevalence depends on price versus quantity competition and on the choice of MARL algorithm, with implications for wireless market design. Producer: Qixuan Zai and Randall Berry; the arXiv abstract page shows version 1 submitted on 15 September 2026 and version 2 on 22 September 2026 (computer science and game theory). Coverage: a generic market model. Access: free PDF and HTML on arXiv; no code was mentioned. Licence and cost: free to read; licence CC-BY-4.0 (the paper, as linked on its arXiv abstract page). Caveats: a very recent unreviewed preprint, and its results depend on the chosen algorithms and market parameters. Simulation uses: it provides an agent-based learning model for testing spectrum-sharing market rules and competition outcomes. Related record: the stochastic geometry model of infrastructure sharing between operators (model-mno-infrastructure-sharing-stochastic-geometry-cournot-market).
